subject: Tenant capsule topology & evidence deliverable
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <security@tritonfinancial.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: network segmentation overview for Dedicated/Private deployment

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this on. Triton is working through our vendor SIG and we need a concise network-level narrative + diagrams that show how Redwood isolates tenant workloads across the three deployment modes (hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, Private/VPC). Specifically we need:  

- A high-level topology diagram showing control plane vs data plane separation for Dedicated and Private (including VPC peering, PrivateLink alternatives, and air-gap notes).
- A tenant boundary/"capsule" diagram that explains how compute, KV caches, and model artifacts are scoped per-tenant.
- Short bullets on: egress controls, KMS boundaries, bastion/jump host pattern, and audit-log collection points.
- Artifacts: a diagram (PDF) and a segregation matrix (CSV) mapping controls to SIG/CAIQ questions.

Can you send a short deliverable (we have a 48h window) and flag any gaps that would trigger additional evidence requests? We can share the SIG questionnaire after you confirm.

Best,
Alex Rivera
Security Manager, Triton Financial
security@tritonfinancial.com

--
Note: Please reply with attachments as separate files; we will ingest into our compliance tracker.

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <security@tritonfinancial.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: network segmentation overview for Dedicated/Private deployment

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. We're preparing a short package that addresses the SIG/CAIQ touchpoints you mentioned. High-level plan:

1) Tenant capsule topology (attached) — PDF with two views: logical (control/data plane separation) and physical (VPC/subnet/east-west controls).
2) Segregation matrix (attached) — CSV mapping architecture elements to SIG questions (network boundaries, egress, key mgmt).
3) Quick notes (inline below) to pre-answer common questions.

Quick bullets:
- Control plane: hosted control plane is multi-tenant but the control plane does NOT have direct access to customer model weights or KV caches; API calls reference tenant-scoped artifacts via opaque identifiers. For Dedicated/Private customers we can deploy a private control plane (VPC-hosted or customer-managed) — see diagram for options.
- Data plane separation: Dedicated uses reserved GPU pools with tenant affinity; each tenant workload runs in isolated containers on hardware pools with encrypted local storage and per-tenant KV namespaces.
- Networking: Private deployments use VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on customer preference; we recommend PrivateLink for tighter egress controls and to avoid cross-account route table complexity.
- Egress and NAT: Egress is blocked by default; only sanctioned egress via ops-approved proxies is allowed. We support egress allow-lists and per-tenant egress auditing.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys supported for Private; Hosted/Dedicated use dedicated keys per-customer in our KMS partitioning model and are logged to audit trail.
- Bastion: Admin access requires jump-host through customer-approved bastions for Private, and through our managed bastions for Dedicated with strict RBAC and JIT access.

Attachments: 
- tenant_capsule_topology_v1.pdf (diagram, 2 pages)
- segregation_matrix.csv (control-to-question mapping)

I am attaching the first draft — Jonas and Kimberly, can you confirm the matrix rows on egress filtering and audit sinks before I send to Triton? I'd like to get this to them by EOD.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Security
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: tenant_capsule_topology_v1.pdf]
[Attachment: segregation_matrix.csv]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 12:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: quick review of segregation matrix rows

Jonas / Kimberly — quick internal note (no external recipients):

- Jonas: please confirm the wording in row 14 ("KV cache namespace enforcement") — we currently state that caches are namespaced AND access-controlled via tokenized ACLs; confirm we can include the recent runtime patch that adds per-namespace caps.
- Kimberly: please validate the audit sink list (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Splunk) and ensure we call out "immutable" log archiving for Private (customer-managed archive option).

If you both can ack with edits inline in the CSV, I'll finalize and send. I flagged a single TODO regarding control-plane key access for Dedicated (we may need to offer a dedicated control-plane KMS partition if Triton insists).

Thanks — Stephanie

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <security@tritonfinancial.com>, procurement@tritonfinancial.com
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 15:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: network segmentation overview for Dedicated/Private deployment

Alex — attaching the requested deliverables. Summary of what we included: 

- tenant_capsule_topology_v1.pdf — two-panel topology: logical control/data plane separation and recommended Private deployment pattern (PrivateLink + customer VPC endpoints). Diagram includes:
  * Control plane endpoints (multi-tenant vs private control plane),
  * Data plane GPU pools with tenant affinity,
  * KV cache namespaces and encryption layers,
  * Audit log flow to immutable buckets and SIEM connectors.
- segregation_matrix.csv — mapping of architecture elements to SIG/CAIQ entries, including where we have policy evidence vs technical evidence.

Notes and open items: 
- KMS: For Private we fully support Customer-Managed Keys via external KMS integrations (options listed in matrix). For Dedicated we provide per-customer key partitions; if Triton requires a physically separated control plane KMS partition we can scope that as an add-on (will need legal/ops signoff).
- Egress: Default-deny outbound with telemetry to per-tenant egress logs. If you need certified firewall appliance screenshots or built rule exports, let us know and we'll include them.
- SOC 2/SIG mapping: matrix flags items that map to SOC 2 common criteria. We can extract specific evidence artifacts (IAM role snapshots, NACL lists) on request.

Attachments: tenant_capsule_topology_v1.pdf, segregation_matrix.csv

Next steps: Please confirm receipt and whether Triton's SIG ingestion requires anything beyond the two files. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the diagram.

Best regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
